title: Aquatic plants picture cards and sorting sheet
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Soils and aquatic plants (Flow and One Planet, Our World)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 31 (Aquatic plants picture cards and sorting sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 31: Aquatic plants. To understand how plants that live in water are suited to their habitat

blocks.title: Sort into: Floating / Submerged / Edge
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Floating, Submerged, Edge.
blocks.answer: Floating: Water lily; Duckweed. Submerged: Pondweed; Water starwort. Edge: Reeds; Bulrush

questions.q: Why are water lily leaves wide and flat?
questions.a: To float and catch as much sunlight as possible
questions.model: Think about the job: leaves need sunlight. On a pond, light comes from above. Wide flat leaves float on top and catch the most light.

questions.q: Is a reed floating, submerged or edge?
Why do pondweed stems bend easily?
questions.a: So they move with the water and do not snap

questions.q: Draw and label a water lily and a pondweed. Write one adaptation beside each.
questions.a: Water lily: wide flat floating leaves, air spaces; pondweed: thin bendy stems, under water
questions.model: Teacher draws the water lily: a flat round leaf on the surface, a long stalk down to the mud, labelled 'wide flat leaf: catches sunlight'.

questions.q: Float a lettuce leaf and a small stone in a bowl of water. Which floats? Why might leaves float?
questions.a: The leaf floats: it is light and thin with air inside

questions.q: Why would a cactus not survive in a pond?
questions.a: It is adapted to store water in a dry place; in a pond its roots would rot and it has no floating or bendy parts.

questions.q: Big question: how does a water lily stay up?
questions.a: Wide flat leaves and air spaces help it float.
